# Part III — Configuring the engine

One chapter for each job the ECU does. Each follows the same shape: what it does, how it works, before you start, setting it up, worked examples, tuning it, diagnostics, troubleshooting and the full settings reference.

- **[15 Engine and vehicle basics](15-engine-vehicle.md)** — The Engine settings tell the ECU what kind of engine it is running: how many cylinders, how big, which cycle, the order they fire in and how the coils and injectors are arranged. The Vehicle settings record which car the tune belongs to.
- **[16 The trigger system](16-trigger.md)** — The trigger system reads the crank and cam sensors, works out exactly where the engine is in its cycle, and refuses to fire anything until it can prove it.
- **[17 Sensors and calibration](17-sensors.md)** — Every input the ECU reads — pressure, temperature, throttle, lambda, switch or speed — is one entry in a catalogue, set up the same way: switch it on, say how it is wired, give it a calibration, and choose which faults it should report.
- **[18 Outputs and the pin system](18-outputs.md)** — Every output pin on the ECU has one row in the tune that says what the pin does: fire a coil, open an injector, or drive a load such as a pump, fan or solenoid from conditions and a value you choose.
- **[19 Fuel](19-fuel.md)** — The fuel system works out how much air each cylinder takes in, how much fuel that air needs for the mixture you asked for, and how long to hold each injector open to deliver it.
- **[20 Ignition](20-ignition.md)** — The Ignition module decides when each spark plug fires and how long each coil charges first, from the advance map, its corrections and every safety retard, inside limits you set.
- **[21 Idle](21-idle.md)** — Idle control gives the engine the air it needs to idle — more when cold, more when the air conditioning comes on — and, in closed loop, trims it until the engine sits on the idle speed you asked for.
- **[22 Electronic throttle](22-electronic-throttle.md)** — Drive-by-wire reads the accelerator pedal, decides where the throttle plate should be, and moves the plate there with a motor — checking both the pedal and the plate with two sensors each, and letting the plate's spring take over the moment anything disagrees.
- **[23 Closed-loop lambda](23-lambda.md)** — Closed loop reads the oxygen sensor and adjusts the fuel until the mixture matches **Target Lambda** — a fast trim that corrects right now, and a learned trim that remembers the correction, cell by cell, on the VE table's own grid.
- **[24 Boost](24-boost.md)** — The Boost module decides how much boost to ask for, drives the wastegate to get it, and cuts the engine if manifold pressure ever goes where it must not.
- **[25 Cam and valve control](25-vvt-vvl.md)** — Cam control moves each camshaft on its phaser to the angle a table asks for, measuring where it really is from the cam sensor, and valve-lift control switches a two-stage cam (VTEC-style) to its high-lift profile at high engine speed.
- **[26 Launch, shift and traction](26-launch-shift-traction.md)** — Launch control holds the engine at a set speed on the line with its own timing and fuel maps, flat shift cuts the engine for a moment so you can change up without lifting, and traction control pulls power when the driven wheels spin faster than the car is moving.
- **[27 Speed limiting](27-speed-limiting.md)** — The rev limiter keeps engine speed under a ceiling, the pit limiter keeps road speed under a ceiling, and cruise control holds a road speed by opening an electronic throttle.
- **[28 Power adders](28-power-adders.md)** — Nitrous and water-methanol injection are switched on inside a safe window of engine speed, throttle and boost, and anti-lag retards the timing hard on a closed throttle to keep a turbo spinning — each one only publishes a signal that you give to an output.
- **[29 Engine protection](29-protection.md)** — The ECU watches for faults — sensors that have died, an engine running too hot, too much boost, a lean mixture, a hot exhaust — records each as a trouble code, and reacts by the severity of the worst one: enriching, retarding, trimming boost, lowering the rev limit, or cutting.
- **[30 Knock](30-knock.md)** — After each cylinder fires, the ECU listens to the knock sensor in a short window, compares what it hears with what that cylinder normally sounds like at that speed and load, and pulls timing from a cylinder that is knocking — and it can spot pre-ignition and cut that cylinder's fuel.
- **[31 Misfire detection](31-misfire.md)** — A cylinder that fires speeds the crank up through its power stroke and one that does not, doesn't — so the ECU times each cylinder's stretch of crank rotation, and a stretch that is noticeably slower than its neighbours is counted as a misfire.
- **[32 Vehicle functions](32-vehicle-functions.md)** — The ECU turns speed-sensor pulses into a road speed, works out the gear from engine speed and road speed, can regulate the alternator's charge voltage, and can estimate the torque the engine is making.
- **[33 CAN configuration](33-can-config.md)** — You describe each CAN frame the ECU sends or reads — its id, its length, and which bits carry which channel with what scaling — and the ECU turns channels into frames and frames into channels.
- **[34 Generic tables and expressions](34-tables-expressions.md)** — Generic tables are eight spare maps you can point anything at, and expressions are short formulas — `clt > 95 and rpm > 800` — that many settings use to decide when something happens or how much.
- **[35 Lua scripting](35-lua.md)** — A Lua script of your own runs on the ECU, reads any channel, writes channels of its own or over the ECU's, and can send and receive CAN frames and raise trouble codes.
- **[36 System settings](36-system.md)** — This chapter is about the ECU as a whole — what it does when it powers up, how a tune is kept, what burning does to a running engine, and what the SD card is for.
